title: Deep ComCat pair order exceeded regional magnitude-shuffle scores in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether regional magnitude distributions can account for a published larger-first excess in deep earthquake pairs. We used 785 ComCat events with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 and depth greater than 300 km in 2000-2025. Pairs were within 200 km hypocentral chord distance and seven days, with a magnitude gap of at least 0.3. We held times and locations fixed and shuffled magnitudes within 10-degree cells, five-year periods and 100-km depth bands. The observed signed count was 50: 81 larger-first pairs out of 112. The mean shuffled score was 2.86. The two-sided Monte Carlo p value was 0.0006 in 19,999 draws. After removal of the first day, the two-sided p value was 0.1412. This tests regional random labeling, not direct triggering or independent magnitudes in a causal point process. The data overlap the prior study. Sparse large events, mixed magnitude scales, missed events, and the chosen shuffle groups limit inference. Original code, aggregate draws, a figure and a separate arithmetic audit are included. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Observed signed pair count and central 95% ranges from magnitude shuffles. These ranges describe the null, not confidence intervals for a physical effect.

citations.reason: Prior magnitude-order result sets the new conditional shuffle question. Data overlap completely.
